re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Title**: gh-994 validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-994` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +522
- **Deletions**: -272
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T19:08:38Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T19:08:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #994
## gh-994: validation_failed park reset on head change

### Root Cause
- The RESET ladder in `update_branch` (js/smAgent.js) never removed the label merely because the head moved: the #633 rung re-checked the new head's dispatched verdict (a kicker push that re-validated red kept the park — fa #156, 20+ min), gh-952 was machine-scoped and verdict-gated, and machine movement hit the `machinePushVf` HOLD. Only a fresh *human* push cleared it — 4 manual deletions on 2026-10-17, each violating the machine's own contract: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

### Fix
- js/smAgent.js: new FIRST-POSITION rung — when the park comment's recorded `parked-head` sha differs from the current `headRefOid` (full-SHA compare; force-push = fast-forward), the label is removed **unconditionally** (no actor/park-time/verdict probes; guests and machine PRs alike) — so kicker, rework-leg, operator and silent merge-main pushes all reset the park. Audit: machine log `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>` only (Q2 default, no PR comment); open-PR cache drop re-arms validate-armed the same tick; same-pass re-park stays suppressed (a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path).
- Removed the dominated #633 verdict-gated rung, the gh-952 outage rung and `clearStalePark952`; parks with no recorded sha keep the legacy human-push/gh-750 probes.
- All machine SET paths now record `parked-head: <sha>` (fail-validation guest/convergence reports, gh-821 zombie park); contract texts made true (I4) in the SET comment, dead-head park body and sm_github.json rule descriptions.

### Test Coverage
- New suite `validation_failed park reset on head change (gh-994)` (5 tests, RED-before-fix on both live shapes): kicker push + red verdict on the new head resets (AC1/AC5, fa #156); guest operator push in a full probe outage resets (AC2, fa #1563); recorded sha == head keeps the park (AC3); two rules racing one tick → exactly one removal, no re-add (AC4); legacy park abstains under dead probes.
- Superseded pins updated: #633 rebase/red-verdict tests, the gh-952 suite, the SET-comment contract assertion, the shared-probe counting test.
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` → 3660 passed, 0 failed; CI node harness (same 153 files) → 3660 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- E3: a manually re-added label without a new park comment still keys on the newest `parked-head:` comment; a differing sha clears it next tick — one bounded removal per tick, no loop.
- E4: a removeLabel failure is caught/warned; the label survives at most one extra turn (retried next tick); the SM turn never crashes.
- Per Q1 the fix lands in the shared agents repo (js/smAgent.js), which both repos' legs resolve.

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

## References

- Live instances 2026-10-17: fa #1563 (3×), fa #1566 (kicker push run 39054011685, head `bf0828c4`).
- Precedent for machine-bug-fix flow: dmtools-agents#969 (rework retry loop fix shipped through the same pipeline).
- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
- The contract sentence being violated, quoted from the machine's own parked-PR comment: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

## Machine jobs

Now let me look at the full js/smAgent.js around the changed region to understand the context — especially: `parkedHeadSha`, `parkResetCommit`, `parkedSince`, `dropOpenPrsCache`, `isMachinePrU`, and the SET paths that record `parked-head`. Also the diff for tests and sm_github.json.

Key observations so far:

1. The new first-position rung removes the label when `uHead !== parkedHeadVf` with NO dispatched-verdict probe. The PR description claims "same-pass re-park stays suppressed (a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path)". Wait — is that true? The SET path for machine PRs re-parks if the new head goes red... but for machine PRs there's a fail-validation report that re-parks. But hold on — a genuinely red new head: the reset fires unconditionally, removes the label. Then does anything re-park it? For machine PRs, the fail-validation path sets the label again when the new head's validation fails. That's one CI cycle later. OK.

But wait — there's a potential issue: a NEW head that has ALREADY gone red (e.g. rework pushed a fix, validation ran and failed on the new head before the SM tick ran). Then the reset removes the label even though the current head is red. The SET path needs to re-park. For guest PRs the SET path runs in the same block (line ~2142, `if (!unparkedThisPass && !isMachinePrU && ...)`). Since unparkedThisPass=true, the same-pass SET is skipped — guest stays unparked until next tick. For machine PRs, the fail-validation report (line ~374) re-parks with parked-head marker. OK per design.

2. Issue: `unparkedThisPass = true` even when `DRY` is true — fine.

3. Potential issue: `parkedHeadSha` — what does it return? It reads the newest `parked-head:` comment. Note E3: a manually re-added label without a new park comment keys on the newest `parked-head:` comment. If the recorded sha differs from the current head, the reset fires. But wait: if the label was manually re-added on the SAME head and the park comment records the same head — reset doesn't fire; but also there's no "keep park" for the same-head case — the label just persists, which is intended (parked on current head).

Hmm, but here's a subtle bug scenario: a PR is parked on head H1. Kicker pushes H2. The reset fires, removes the label. But if the removal fails (E4), next tick the reset fires again — fine.

4. Bigger issue — the check `headChangeResetVf = !!(uHead && parkedHeadVf && uHead !== parkedHeadVf)`. `parkedHeadSha` returns the sha from the newest park comment. If that sha equals the current head, keep park — intended. But what if `parkedHeadSha` returns a sha from a NON-park comment? E.g., the dead-head park body (gh-922) includes `parked-head: <sha>` — but in that case the head branch no longer exists, so uHead would be null and the reset doesn't fire. OK.

5. Now a real concern: the unconditional reset fires BEFORE any check that the label was set by the machine vs. manually by a human. Per ticket, that's by design.

6. Look at the `parked-head` marker added in the fail-validation report: `(((convergencePark || !isMachinePr) && failHead) ? '\nparked-head: ' + failHead : '')`. For machine PRs (non-convergence), no parked-head marker is recorded in the fail-validation report! The condition is `(convergencePark || !isMachinePr) && failHead`. For a regular machine PR fail-validation (not convergence), `!isMachinePr` is false and `convergencePark` is false → no marker. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 999

- **Title**: gh-994 validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-994` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +522
- **Deletions**: -272
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T19:08:38Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T19:08:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #994
## gh-994: validation_failed park reset on head change

### Root Cause
- The RESET ladder in `update_branch` (js/smAgent.js) never removed the label merely because the head moved: the #633 rung re-checked the new head's dispatched verdict (a kicker push that re-validated red kept the park — fa #156, 20+ min), gh-952 was machine-scoped and verdict-gated, and machine movement hit the `machinePushVf` HOLD. Only a fresh *human* push cleared it — 4 manual deletions on 2026-10-17, each violating the machine's own contract: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

### Fix
- js/smAgent.js: new FIRST-POSITION rung — when the park comment's recorded `parked-head` sha differs from the current `headRefOid` (full-SHA compare; force-push = fast-forward), the label is removed **unconditionally** (no actor/park-time/verdict probes; guests and machine PRs alike) — so kicker, rework-leg, operator and silent merge-main pushes all reset the park. Audit: machine log `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>` only (Q2 default, no PR comment); open-PR cache drop re-arms validate-armed the same tick; same-pass re-park stays suppressed (a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path).
- Removed the dominated #633 verdict-gated rung, the gh-952 outage rung and `clearStalePark952`; parks with no recorded sha keep the legacy human-push/gh-750 probes.
- All machine SET paths now record `parked-head: <sha>` (fail-validation guest/convergence reports, gh-821 zombie park); contract texts made true (I4) in the SET comment, dead-head park body and sm_github.json rule descriptions.

### Test Coverage

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

## References

- Live instances 2026-10-17: fa #1563 (3×), fa #1566 (kicker push run 39054011685, head `bf0828c4`).
- Precedent for machine-bug-fix flow: dmtools-agents#969 (rework retry loop fix shipped through the same pipeline).
- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
- The contract sentence being violated, quoted from the machine's own parked-PR comment: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

Now let me look at the full js/smAgent.js around the changed region to understand the context — especially: `parkedHeadSha`, `parkResetCommit`, `parkedSince`, `dropOpenPrsCache`, `isMachinePrU`, and the SET paths that record `parked-head`. Also the diff for tests and sm_github.json.

Key observations so far:

1. The new first-position rung removes the label when `uHead !== parkedHeadVf` with NO dispatched-verdict probe. The PR description claims "same-pass re-park stays suppressed (a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path)". Wait — is that true? The SET path for machine PRs re-parks if the new head goes red... but for machine PRs there's a fail-validation report that re-parks. But hold on — a genuinely red new head: the reset fires unconditionally, removes the label. Then does anything re-park it? For machine PRs, the fail-validation path sets the label again when the new head's validation fails. That's one CI cycle later. OK.

But wait — there's a potential issue: a NEW head that has ALREADY gone red (e.g. rework pushed a fix, validation ran and failed on the new head before the SM tick ran). Then the reset removes the label even though the current head is red. The SET path needs to re-park. For guest PRs the SET path runs in the same block (line ~2142, `if (!unparkedThisPass && !isMachinePrU && ...)`). Since unparkedThisPass=true, the same-pass SET is skipped — guest stays unparked until next tick. For machine PRs, the fail-validation report (line ~374) re-parks with parked-head marker. OK per design.

2. Issue: `unparkedThisPass = true` even when `DRY` is true — fine.

3. Potential issue: `parkedHeadSha` — what does it return? It reads the newest `parked-head:` comment. Note E3: a manually re-added label without a new park comment keys on the newest `parked-head:` comment. If the recorded sha differs from the current head, the reset fires. But wait: if the label was manually re-added on the SAME head and the park comment records the same head — reset doesn't fire; but also there's no "keep park" for the same-head case — the label just persists, which is intended (parked on current head).

Hmm, but here's a subtle bug scenario: a PR is parked on head H1. Kicker pushes H2. The reset fires, removes the label. But if the removal fails (E4), next tick the reset fires again — fine.

4. Bigger issue — the check `headChangeResetVf = !!(uHead && parkedHeadVf && uHead !== parkedHeadVf)`. `parkedHeadSha` returns the sha from the newest park comment. If that sha equals the current head, keep park — intended. But what if `parkedHeadSha` returns a sha from a NON-park comment? E.g., the dead-head park body (gh-922) includes `parked-head: <sha>` — but in that case the head branch no longer exists, so uHead would be null and the reset doesn't fire. OK.

5. Now a real concern: the unconditional reset fires BEFORE any check that the label was set by the machine vs. manually by a human. Per ticket, that's by design.

6. Look at the `parked-head` marker added in the fail-validation report: `(((convergencePark || !isMachinePr) && failHead) ? '\nparked-head: ' + failHead : '')`. For machine PRs (non-convergence), no parked-head marker is recorded in the fail-validation report! The condition is `(convergencePark || !isMachinePr) && failHead`. For a regular machine PR fail-validation (not convergence), `!isMachinePr` is false and `convergencePark` is false → no marker. Hmm, but the PR description says "All machine SET paths now record `parked-head: <sha>` (fail-validation guest/convergence reports...)". So for machine PRs, the park is set by other paths? Wait — do machine PRs get the validation_failed label at all from the fail-validation path? Earlier comment said "Machine PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads; they re-enter on a new head as today)". Actually machine PRs fail-validation report doesn't park them with the label... except convergence park and guest. Hmm, but there was gh-821 zombie park which is machine? The zombie park now records the marker.

But wait — for machine PRs, who sets the label? The dead-head park (gh-922) records `parked-head: <headSha>` already. The zombie park now records it. The fail-validation path only sets label for guests... Actually `convergencePark` for machine PRs sets the label. OK.

But there could be an asymetry: the marker only included when `(convergencePark || !isMachinePr)`. For a machine PR non-convergence fail, no label is set (per earlier comment), so no marker needed. Fine.

7. Now the concern about the dead-head park (gh-922): the branch no longer exists, uHead is null → headChangeResetVf false → legacy ladder → parkResetCommit(uHead=null)... `actorVf = uHead ? ... : null` → null → warn fail-closed. Same as before. OK.

8. Concern: removal of gh-952 rung and `clearStalePark952` — the gh-952 suite tests updated. Fine.

9. Potential BUG: In the new head-change reset path, when the head changed, the label is removed — but the "park comment" with `parked-head:` marker remains. Next tick, `parkedHeadSha` still finds that old comment. But the label is gone, so no issue. But E3: label manually re-added → next tick, parkedHeadSha = old H1, current head H2 differs → reset fires again and removes it. The PR says "one bounded removal per tick, no loop" — acceptable per design.

10. A more serious potential bug: `parkedHeadSha` scans for the NEWEST `parked-head:` comment. Consider scenario: PR parked on H1 (marker H1). Head moves to H2, reset fires, label removed, no new comment (Q2: log only). Then the PR goes red on H2 — fail-validation SET path re-parks with marker H2. Good. Then head moves to H3 → reset. Fine.

But consider: PR parked on H1. Kicker pushes H2 which is red. Reset fires (removes label). Same tick, `unparkedThisPass` suppresses guest re-park. For machine PR: does the SET path run same pass? The fail-validation report is generated where? Line 374 area is a different code path (fail-validation report), not gated on unparkedThisPass? Actually that line is in a different rule processing maybe. The PR says "a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path". OK.

Now, the real important check: does the SET path for the *guest* park only trigger when checks are red and unparkedThisPass is false? Yes: `if (!unparkedThisPass && !isMachinePrU && ...)` at line ~2142.

11. Now check whether `parkedHeadSha` and `parkResetCommit` handle things correctly — read the current file. Also verify the tests file diff and sm_github.json diff. Also check AGENTS.md conventions. Also there's no ci_failures.md input — meaning CI passed presumably.

12. One thing to verify: `headChangeResetVf` uses `uHead` — what is uHead? Probably current head sha of the PR. And it compares full SHAs — good.

Potential issue: case sensitivity? SHAs from GitHub API are lowercase; fine.

13. Concern about `dropOpenPrsCache(effectiveRepoInfo)` being called even in DRY mode? It's inside `if (headChangeResetVf)` but outside `if (!DRY)`. In DRY mode, we didn't remove the label but drop the cache — cache drop is harmless (just re-query). Fine.

14. Performance: `parkedHeadSha` is called for every parked PR — presumably reads comments. It was already called before the change in some paths; now it's called unconditionally for every label-present PR. It was called before too (var parkedHeadVf = parkedHeadSha(...) at the same place). OK.

15. Possible issue: legacy parks now do the `parkedHeadSha` call first (comment scan) then the legacy probes. Before, `parkedHeadSha` was also computed at top. Same cost.

16. Now the machineUnpark (gh-750) rung for machine PRs: it's now only reachable when parkedHeadVf is null/'' OR equals uHead. For machine PRs whose park comment records a sha that differs, the first rung fires. When sha matches current head (parked on the head being validated), the legacy ladder runs and gh-750 can still clear if rollup green or head moved... wait, if parkedHeadVf === uHead, headMovedCleanVf requires headTs > parkedTs — head commit date > park time even when sha unchanged? Edge. Fine.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

## PR Description

Closes #994
## gh-994: validation_failed park reset on head change

### Root Cause
- The RESET ladder in `update_branch` (js/smAgent.js) never removed the label merely because the head moved: the #633 rung re-checked the new head's dispatched verdict (a kicker push that re-validated red kept the park — fa #156, 20+ min), gh-952 was machine-scoped and verdict-gated, and machine movement hit the `machinePushVf` HOLD. Only a fresh *human* push cleared it — 4 manual deletions on 2026-10-17, each violating the machine's own contract: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

### Fix
- js/smAgent.js: new FIRST-POSITION rung — when the park comment's recorded `parked-head` sha differs from the current `headRefOid` (full-SHA compare; force-push = fast-forward), the label is removed **unconditionally** (no actor/park-time/verdict probes; guests and machine PRs alike) — so kicker, rework-leg, operator and silent merge-main pushes all reset the park. Audit: machine log `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>` only (Q2 default, no PR comment); open-PR cache drop re-arms validate-armed the same tick; same-pass re-park stays suppressed (a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path).
- Removed the dominated #633 verdict-gated rung, the gh-952 outage rung and `clearStalePark952`; parks with no recorded sha keep the legacy human-push/gh-750 probes.
- All machine SET paths now record `parked-head: <sha>` (fail-validation guest/convergence reports, gh-821 zombie park); contract texts made true (I4) in the SET comment, dead-head park body and sm_github.json rule descriptions.

### Test Coverage
- New suite `validation_failed park reset on head change (gh-994)` (5 tests, RED-before-fix on both live shapes): kicker push + red verdict on the new head resets (AC1/AC5, fa #156); guest operator push in a full probe outage resets (AC2, fa #1563); recorded sha == head keeps the park (AC3); two rules racing one tick → exactly one removal, no re-add (AC4); legacy park abstains under dead probes.
- Superseded pins updated: #633 rebase/red-verdict tests, the gh-952 suite, the SET-comment contract assertion, the shared-probe counting test.
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` → 3660 passed, 0 failed; CI node harness (same 153 files) → 3660 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- E3: a manually re-added label without a new park comment still keys on the newest `parked-head:` comment; a differing sha clears it next tick — one bounded removal per tick, no loop.
- E4: a removeLabel failure is caught/warned; the label survives at most one extra turn (retried next tick); the SM turn never crashes.
- Per Q1 the fix lands in the shared agents repo (js/smAgent.js), which both repos' legs resolve.

blocks.text:
# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

## References

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR re…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 999
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/999
- **Title**: gh-994 validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-994` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +522
- **Deletions**: -272
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T19:08:38Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T19:08:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #994
## gh-994: validation_failed park reset on head change

### Root Cause
- The RESET ladder in `update_branch` (js/smAgent.js) never removed the label merely because the head moved: the #633 rung re-checked the new head's dispatched verdict (a kicker push that re-validated red kept the park — fa #156, 20+ min), gh-952 was machine-scoped and verdict-gated, and machine movement hit the `machinePushVf` HOLD. Only a fresh *human* push cleared it — 4 manual deletions on 2026-10-17, each violating the machine's own contract: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

### Fix
- js/smAgent.js: new FIRST-POSITION rung — when the park comment's recorded `parked-head` sha differs from the current `headRefOid` (full-SHA compare; force-push = fast-forward), the label is removed **unconditionally** (no actor/park-time/verdict probes; guests and machine PRs alike) — so kicker, rework-leg, operator and silent merge-main pushes all reset the park. Audit: machine log `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>` only (Q2 default, no PR comment); open-PR cache drop re-arms validate-armed the same tick; same-pass re-park stays suppressed (a red new head re-parks one cycle later via the SET path).
- Removed the dominated #633 verdict-gated rung, the gh-952 outage rung and `clearStalePark952`; parks with no recorded sha keep the legacy human-push/gh-750 probes.
- All machine SET paths now record `parked-head: <sha>` (fail-validation guest/convergence reports, gh-821 zombie park); contract texts made true (I4) in the SET comment, dead-head park body and sm_github.json rule descriptions.

### Test Coverage
- New suite `validation_failed park reset on head change (gh-994)` (5 tests, RED-before-fix on both live shapes): kicker push + red verdict on the new head resets (AC1/AC5, fa #156); guest operator push in a full probe outage resets (AC2, fa #1563); recorded sha == head keeps the park (AC3); two rules racing one tick → exactly one removal, no re-add (AC4); legacy park abstains under dead probes.
- Superseded pins updated: #633 rebase/red-verdict tests, the gh-952 suite, the SET-comment contract assertion, the shared-probe counting test.
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` → 3660 passed, 0 failed; CI node harness (same 153 files) → 3660 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes
- E3: a manually re-added label without a new park comment still keys on the newest `parked-head:` comment; a differing sha clears it next tick — one bounded removal per tick, no loop.
- E4: a removeLabel failure is caught/warned; the label survives at most one extra turn (retried next tick); the SM turn never crashes.
- Per Q1 the fix lands in the shared agents repo (js/smAgent.js), which both repos' legs resolve.
